newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian Hermis Bank swings to 1996 profit.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian Hermis Bank swings to 1996 profit.

text.p: One of Lithuania's leading commercial banks, Hermis Bank, said on Thursday that its audited 1996 results showed a net profit of 27.4 million litas after an eight million litas loss in 1995.
The bank, more than 75 percent owned by foreign investors, was optimistic that it would boost its 1997 profit.

"The profit will be higher than 1996 since in the first two and a half months of this year we are already showing an 8.5 million litas net profit," Hermis chairwoman Nadyezhda Novickiene told Reuters.
The bank said in a statement that it was the most profitable bank in Lithuania and that it would probably pay dividends again this year.
The share capital of Hermis increased threefold in 1996 and is now 67 million litas, the bank added.
The assets of the bank in 1996 rose by 68 percent to 534 milion litas at the end of the year.
The bank said that net credits issued rose by 52 percent to 198 million litas from 130 million litas, which it said was due to a conservative credit policy.
It said capital adequacy at end 1996 was 23.4 percent, nearly three times more than needed under central bank rules.
The number of clients and turnover rose, leading to a rise of clients' funds held in bank accounts from 253 million litas to 395 million litas, the bank added.
The bank said that it provided more sophisticated services, leading to a doubling of bank services revenue.
